description.value: The study examined whether individual differences in emotion regulation success predict pain regulation success and whether amygdalar activity reflects regulatory success across emotion and pain paradigms.

spans.text: To test whether individual differences in emotion regulation success predict pain regulation success

value: We hypothesized that individuals with greater ability to regulate negative emotion would also be more successful when regulating their responses to painful stimuli.

Given that affect regulation and the emotional modulation of pain both target the amygdala, we further hypothesized that changes in amygdalar activity following regulation would reflect individual differences in regulatory success in both emotion and pain domains.

spans.text: We hypothesized that individuals with greater ability to regulate negative emotion would also be more successful when regulating their responses to painful stimuli.

description.value: Longitudinal study with three assessments over approximately three years, including two emotion regulation sessions and one pain regulation session.

spans.text: To test whether individual differences in emotion regulation success predict pain regulation success, we tested the same individuals three times over an approximately 3-year period
In all three sessions participants were instructed to either decrease (“suppress”) or increase (“enhance”) their emotional responses to the aversive stimuli
emotion regulation session 1
Individuals came to the laboratory twice to participate in voluntary emotion regulation tasks, one in which peripheral-physiological data were collected (session 1)
one where neuroimaging data were collected (session 2)
pain regulation session
Individuals returned a third time to the laboratory to participate in a voluntary pain regulation task when neuroimaging, peripheral-physiological and behavioral data were collected (session 3)

definition.value: The results of a whole-brain voxelwise correlation between change in corrugator EMG activity (enhance – suppress) and BOLD signal for the corresponding contrast during the emotion regulation task.

spans.text: The results of a whole-brain voxelwise correlation between change in corrugator EMG activity (enhance – suppress) and BOLD signal for the corresponding contrast during the emotion regulation task replicated the previously demonstrated role of the amygdala: BOLD signal changes in left amygdala were significantly correlated with changes in emotion regulatory success as indexed by corrugator EMG (activation in other regions was also correlated with changes in emotion regulation success; for a complete listing, see Table 1 ).

The results of a whole-brain voxelwise correlation between change in corrugator EMG activity (enhance – suppress) and BOLD signal for the corresponding contrast during the emotion regulation task replicated the previously demonstrated role of the amygdala: BOLD signal changes in left amygdala were significantly correlated with changes in emotion regulatory success as indexed by corrugator EMG (activation in other regions was also correlated with changes in emotion regulation success; for a complete listing, see Table 1 ).
Seventeen participants met this criterion and hence constituted the final sample retained for the current investigation.
All coordinates are reported in MNI space.

definition.value: The voxelwise correlation between change in pain unpleasantness ratings (enhance – suppress) and BOLD signal for the enhance – suppress contrast during the pain regulation task across the whole brain.

spans.text: Similarly, the voxelwise correlation between change in pain unpleasantness ratings (enhance – suppress) and BOLD signal for the enhance – suppress contrast during the pain regulation task across the whole brain confirmed the hypothesized role of the amygdala in pain regulation: BOLD signal changes in bilateral amygdala were significantly correlated with changes in regulatory success (for a complete listing of all regions whose activation correlated with changes in pain regulation success, see Table 2 ).

Similarly, the voxelwise correlation between change in pain unpleasantness ratings (enhance – suppress) and BOLD signal for the enhance – suppress contrast during the pain regulation task across the whole brain confirmed the hypothesized role of the amygdala in pain regulation: BOLD signal changes in bilateral amygdala were significantly correlated with changes in regulatory success (for a complete listing of all regions whose activation correlated with changes in pain regulation success, see Table 2 ).
Seventeen participants met this criterion and hence constituted the final sample retained for the current investigation.
All coordinates are reported in MNI space.

functional images were acquired sagittally using whole-brain echo-planar imaging (EPI)
Functional and anatomical data were acquired with a 3.0 T GE scanner (GE Medical Systems, Waukesha, WI) using a quadrature head coil.

After the anatomical images were collected, functional images were acquired sagittally using whole-brain echo-planar imaging (EPI), with 30 slices of 4 mm of thickness (1 mm interslice gap; TE = 30 ms; TR= 2 s; flip angle = 90°; FOV = 240 × 240; 64 × 64 matrix).

spans.text: Preprocessing steps included highpass filtering at 100s, FILM correction for autocorrelation in the BOLD signal, motion correction using MCFLIRT and creation of a confound matrix of points of outlier-intensity changes left uncorrected by MCFLIRT to be used as regressors of non-interest in the analyses, thus removing movement-confounded activation.

Emotion Regulation Sessions

description.value: Participants regulated their emotional responses to negative pictures by imagining better or worse outcomes.

spans.text: During the suppress condition, participants decreased their emotional response to a negative picture by reappraising it as less negative
negative picture

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to regulate their emotional responses to negative pictures by cognitively reappraising them: in the suppress condition, imagining a better or less negative outcome, and in the enhance condition, imagining a worse or more negative outcome. Regulation began 4 seconds after picture onset and continued until the cue to relax.

spans.text: In the enhance condition, participants increased their emotional response by reappraising the image as more negative

Pain Regulation Session

description.value: Participants regulated their responses to painful thermal stimuli by imagining positive or threatening outcomes.

spans.text: Participants were familiarized with the thermal stimulation in the fMRI environment by undergoing a simulation session in a mock scanner.
Painful heat was delivered to the non-dominant left forearm
participants rated pain intensity and unpleasantness on 11-point Likert scales

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to regulate their responses to painful thermal stimulation using cognitive reappraisal: in the suppress condition, imagining the heat represented a good or more positive outcome, and in the enhance condition, imagining it represented a threat to life and well-being. On some trials they were instructed to respond normally.

spans.text: In the suppress condition, participants imagined the heat represented a good outcome
